record.paper_title: A modified star formation law as a solution to open problems in galaxy evolution
record.original_question: Can a single high-resolution semi-analytic model of galaxy formation simultaneously match the observed specific-star-formation-rate--stellar-mass relation at redshift z = 0, the stellar mass function and its evolution, galaxy two-point correlation functions, and galaxy cold-gas fractions? The model must do this without relying on unrestricted tuning of all physical recipes and while keeping its star-formation, feedback, cooling, and merging prescriptions physically plausible.

evidence.quote:
Up to now, a high-resolution SAM that matches
the SSFR-stellar mass relation at z = 0, the SMF and
its evolution, the correlation functions and the cold gas
fractions of galaxies simultaneously, does not yet seem to
exist.

These results show again that
it is currently diﬃcult for a single model to ﬁt all observa-
tions, as mentioned in Sec. 1, unless we allow for free tuning
of all recipes, including cooling (see NW2010).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider semi-analytic models (SAMs) of galaxy formation built on top of high-resolution cosmological N-body merger trees. Such a model evolves baryons within dark-matter halos using prescriptions for (i) gas cooling from a hot halo onto a central galaxy, (ii) star formation from a cold gas reservoir, (iii) energetic feedback from supernovae and active galactic nuclei, and (iv) galaxy mergers triggered by dynamical friction. For each galaxy at redshift z the model predicts a stellar mass M_*, a star-formation rate SFR, and a cold gas mass M_cold.

Define the following observables:
- The specific-star-formation-rate–stellar-mass relation at z = 0: the locus of SSFR = SFR/M_* as a function of M_* for star-forming galaxies.
- The galaxy stellar mass function (SMF): the comoving number density Φ(M_*, z) dlog M_* of galaxies, and its evolution with z.
- The galaxy two-point correlation function ξ(r) (or its projected analog w_p(r_p)) measuring spatial clustering as a function of separation r.
- The cold-gas fraction f_gas = M_cold/(M_cold + M_*) as a function of stellar mass.

Question: Does there exist a single high-resolution semi-analytic model of galaxy formation, with star-formation, feedback, cooling, and merging prescriptions that remain physically plausible (in particular, without unrestricted simultaneous tuning of all recipes), whose predictions simultaneously reproduce, within current observational uncertainties, all of the following: the observed SSFR–M_* relation at z = 0, the observed SMF and its redshift evolution, the observed galaxy two-point correlation functions, and the observed cold-gas fractions of galaxies?
artifact.status_search_result: Reviews and recent SAM studies indicate that simultaneously matching the SSFR–M_* relation at z=0, the stellar mass function and its evolution, galaxy clustering, and cold-gas fractions with a single physically motivated, high-resolution semi-analytic model remains an active challenge. Different SAMs calibrated to the SMF give widely diverging predictions for SSFR and gas fractions, and known tensions persist (e.g., low-mass galaxies overproduced at high z, gas-fraction discrepancies). No published model is broadly recognized as having met all four constraints without aggressive multi-recipe tuning.

status_evidence.title: Star formation in semi-analytic galaxy formation models with multiphase gas
status_evidence.snippet: Predictions for SMFs, sSFR, gas depletion times, and gas/stellar metallicities are compared; tensions remain across observables.
status_evidence.claim: Matching multiple galaxy observables simultaneously continues to be an active and partially unresolved problem in SAMs.

status_evidence.title: Testing galaxy formation models with galaxy stellar mass functions
status_evidence.snippet: Different models tuned to match SMFs make vastly different predictions for other observables such as SSFR and gas content.
status_evidence.claim: Even SAMs calibrated to the SMF do not consistently match SSFR and cold gas fractions simultaneously.

status_evidence.title: Physical Models of Galaxy Formation in a Cosmological Framework (Somerville & Davé)
status_evidence.snippet: Review notes persistent tensions between SAM predictions for star formation histories, gas content, and clustering.
status_evidence.claim: The simultaneous-match problem is acknowledged as open in recent reviews.
